canonical_statement: SOLARIS evaluated whether adding high-dose vitamin D3 to standard first-line chemotherapy plus bevacizumab improves progression-free survival compared with standard-dose vitamin D3 in previously untreated metastatic colorectal cancer.

Eligible adults had histologically confirmed unresectable locally advanced or metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma, measurable disease by RECIST 1.1, ECOG performance status 0 or 1, and adequate organ function.

population.label: Trial-eligible adults
inclusion_criteria: Histologically confirmed unresectable locally advanced or metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma

canonical_statement: Key exclusions included mismatch repair-deficient or microsatellite instability-high tumors, prior systemic therapy for advanced/metastatic disease, recent hypercalcemia or hypercalcemia-predisposing conditions, recent symptomatic genitourinary stones, concurrent thiazides or calcium supplements, and vitamin D intake of at least 2000 IU/day in the prior year.

population.label: Trial-eligible adults
exclusion_criteria: Prior systemic therapy for advanced/metastatic disease
Hypercalcemia in prior 6 months or predisposing condition in prior 5 years
Symptomatic genitourinary stones in prior year
Vitamin D intake >=2000 IU/day in prior year

canonical_statement: The trial randomized 455 patients; median age was 59 years and 181 (39.8%) were female.
All participants received investigator-selected mFOLFOX6 or FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab 5 mg/kg intravenously on day 1 of each 14-day cycle; bevacizumab could be omitted during cycle 1.

exposures.details: mFOLFOX6 or FOLFIRI backbone; bevacizumab 5 mg/kg IV day 1 every 14 days; bevacizumab could be omitted cycle 1

canonical_statement: The high-dose vitamin D3 group received 8000 IU/day during cycle 1 and 4000 IU/day thereafter.

exposures.details: Reduced to 4000 IU/day in subsequent cycles

canonical_statement: The standard-dose group received vitamin D3 400 IU/day beginning in cycle 1, with a matching placebo capsule during cycle 1 to preserve blinding.

exposures.details: Matching placebo capsule during cycle 1

canonical_statement: Randomization used a 1:1 Pocock-Simon dynamic allocation algorithm stratified by chemotherapy backbone, primary tumor location, and ECOG performance status.
SOLARIS was double-blinded; the research pharmacist was the only study personnel member unblinded to vitamin D3 assignment.
The primary outcome was progression-free survival from randomization until RECIST 1.1 disease progression or death from any cause.

outcome.definition: Time from randomization to RECIST 1.1 progression or death from any cause

canonical_statement: Secondary outcomes included objective response rate, overall survival, baseline vitamin D deficiency, serial plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations, and safety.

concept.text: Secondary efficacy, biomarker, and safety outcomes

canonical_statement: Plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D was measured at baseline, after cycles 4 and 8, and at treatment discontinuation by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry in a single batch; 10% blinded duplicates yielded a coefficient of variation of 5.96%.

The revised target sample size was 445 patients with 273 progression-free survival events, providing 90% power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.70 using a 1-sided log-rank alpha of .05; the sample-size target was increased from 400 because of higher-than-expected nondifferential dropout.

The protocol specified one futility analysis at approximately 50% of progression-free survival events; the trial continued after the interim 1-sided P value of .186 did not cross the futility boundary of .568.

For the primary outcome, median progression-free survival was 11.8 months with high-dose vitamin D3 and 10.3 months with standard-dose vitamin D3; the hazard ratio was 0.92 (95% CI, 0.73-1.16; 1-sided P=.25).

canonical_statement: The investigators concluded that adding high-dose vitamin D3 to standard chemotherapy plus bevacizumab did not improve progression-free survival and should not be recommended for unselected patients with previously untreated metastatic colorectal cancer.
The tested chemotherapy backbones were limited to mFOLFOX6 or FOLFIRI with bevacizumab, which limits generalizability to other first-line regimens.

Use of nonprotocol vitamin D supplements could not be completely excluded, although separation in serial plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations between groups argued against substantial contamination.
